steps.label: Trigger: date stated in the court’s order. Matter event: Scheduling order, p. 2.
Use the date stated in the order, p. 2: “Trial ready date: June 14, 2027.” No calendar roll applies.
Final due date
Trigger: date stated in the court’s order. Matter event: Scheduling order, p. 1.
Use the date stated in the order, p. 1: “Expert disclosures: February 1, 2027.” No calendar roll applies.
Final due date
Trigger: the date set for trial or for the case to be ready for trial. Matter event: Trial ready date.
Exclude the trigger day; count every intervening calendar day, including weekends and holidays.
Count backward from the date set for trial or for the case to be ready for trial; a weekend or holiday landing moves earlier.
Use the federal legal-holiday calendar.
Subtract 90 days; landing day is Tuesday.
The landing day is neither a weekend nor a legal holiday; no calendar roll is required.
Final due date
Trigger: the date set for trial. Matter event: Trial ready date.
Exclude the trigger day; count every intervening calendar day, including weekends and holidays.
Count backward from the date set for trial; a weekend or holiday landing moves earlier.
Use the federal legal-holiday calendar.
Subtract 30 days; landing day is Saturday.
Weekend/holiday landing on Saturday: move earlier to Friday.
Final due date
Trigger: the pretrial disclosures are made. Matter event: Federal pretrial disclosures.
Exclude the trigger day; count every intervening calendar day, including weekends and holidays.
Use the federal legal-holiday calendar.
Add 14 days; landing day is Friday.
The landing day is neither a weekend nor a legal holiday; no calendar roll is required.
